title: Cell Natural Orbitals in Quantum Materials
authors: Harshitra Mahalingam, Nishchhal Verma, Daniel Muñoz-Segovia, Raquel Queiroz
abstract: Understanding correlated quantum matter starts with an accurate model of the single-particle states that interact at low energies: their dispersion, band geometry, orbital content and charge density. In many cases, notably the topological bands of moire materials, it is not straightforward to find a real-space description with a few local orbitals that accomplishes this task. Here we provide a systematic way to identify the local degrees of freedom that best capture the band geometry and charge density of any chosen set of bands. We use the unit-cell one-particle reduced density matrix (UC-1pRDM), obtained by restricting the projector onto the target bands to a single unit cell. Its eigenstates, which we call cell natural orbitals (CNOs), form a local, symmetric basis uniquely determined by the Bloch wavefunctions and the choice of real-space partition. Their eigenvalues measure the occupation of each CNO in the target bands, quantifying entanglement across unit-cell boundaries and the importance of multi-orbital character. A set of CNOs that maximizes total spectral weight and reproduces the target band symmetries provides optimal trial states for Wannierization. We exemplify this by constructing a lattice model for twisted bilayer WSe$_2$ that tracks the orbital content across twist angles.
summary: The paper presents Cell Natural Orbitals (CNOs) as a systematic technique to derive optimal local orbital descriptions directly from the band structure of quantum materials. By analyzing the unit-cell reduced density matrix, CNOs quantify orbital content and entanglement across unit cells. This method offers a robust way to build minimal effective models for studying correlated and topological phenomena in systems like moiré TMDs.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a systematic method to identify local degrees of freedom (orbitals) that accurately capture the band geometry and charge density of target bands in complex quantum materials.
main_result: The authors introduce Cell Natural Orbitals (CNOs), derived from the unit-cell one-particle reduced density matrix, which provide an intrinsic, symmetry-respecting basis for constructing optimal local models.
method: The methodology centers on calculating and diagonalizing the Unit-Cell One-Particle Reduced Density Matrix (UC-1pRDM) to extract CNOs and their associated occupation numbers.
model_or_system: The work applies to correlated quantum matter, particularly focusing on moiré materials like twisted bilayer WSe2, where simple real-space descriptions of topological bands are challenging.
key_observables: CNO eigenvalues ($\lambda_a$) quantify orbital occupation and unit-cell entanglement; the method also analyzes symmetry constraints via irreducible representations (irreps).
important_parameters: Twist angle (in moiré systems), band symmetries, and the choice of real-space partition are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that a suitable real-space partition exists to define the UC-1pRDM; the method aims to overcome limitations in traditional Wannierization techniques regarding topological obstructions.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the construction using $L = \Pi P \Pi$ leading to CNOs and occupations, and show how different unit-cell partitions yield distinct CNOs and envelope functions over the Brillouin zone for TMD examples.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the UC-1pRDM as a tool to derive local orbitals from the band manifold itself, detailing the mathematical construction, analyzing physical diagnostics like entanglement entropy, and demonstrating its utility in modeling moiré systems.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical framework for mapping complex Bloch wavefunctions onto minimal, localized orbital bases, which is crucial input for subsequent correlated electron simulations (e.g., Hubbard models) used in AMO or strongly correlated physics.

The CNOs provide compact local orbitals labeled by their symmetry and Wyckoff position, while the occupations rank their importance within the target bands.
